## Substantive outcome research brief

- Published title: **How AgentSight observes AI agent sessions inside Docker**.
- Canonical route: `/blog/observe-ai-agent-sessions-in-docker/`.
- Reader problem: a development container can hold the authoritative native agent history, provider CLI state, and credentials while the AgentSight Node/UI runs on the host. The reader needs to understand how `agentsight bind --docker-container NAME` crosses that boundary and which trust assumptions remain.
- Decision supported: use Docker-backed `bind` to expose existing native session state from a trusted named container without copying provider credentials to the host; treat Docker daemon access as a separate broad host authority; use Linux `record`/tracing when the question is independent system-level effects rather than native session history.

### Semantic overlap and information gain

- Existing Product, Architecture, Changelog, and `llms.txt` summarize the Docker-backed session feature and its high-level trust boundary.
- No dedicated indexed page previously owned the source-level reader question above.
- The new article adds information not present in those summaries: the three-operation JSONL protocol; exact frame/message/time limits; one bridge process per configured container; user/workdir/home reconstruction; multi-container conflict handling; fail-closed lookup when a peer is unavailable; saved-DB/live-source exclusion; the Codex external-sandbox consequence; and the distinction between the AgentSight named-container allowlist and underlying Docker daemon authority.

### Primary evidence

- AgentSight v1.0.30 `docs/usage.md`: operator contract, supported native providers, credential locality, Codex container sandbox boundary, Docker socket warning, version matching, labels/fallbacks.
- AgentSight v1.0.30 `collector/src/server/container_bridge.rs`: JSONL methods, 8 MiB frame cap, 30-second operation timeout, one-second bridge lock timeout, 10-second Docker command timeout, 65,536-byte message cap, multi-container fan-out, conflict/error behavior, validated `docker exec -i` construction.
- AgentSight v1.0.30 `collector/src/cmd_bind.rs`: saved captures reject Docker live session sources because saved captures are read-only.
- Product PR `#195`: implementation and validation history for Docker-backed native sessions.
- Docker official `docker exec` documentation: user/workdir/environment execution controls.
- Docker official security documentation: control of the Docker daemon is a high-authority host capability; rootless operation is a distinct mitigation boundary.

### Claims explicitly avoided

- Docker-backed native sessions are not described as an independent system trace of every process/file/network effect.
- Keeping provider credentials inside the container is not described as keeping all session content inside the container; parsed session evidence intentionally crosses the bridge to the host Node.
- `--docker-container` is not described as least-privilege Docker authorization; it constrains AgentSight behavior on top of the Docker authority already granted to the host client.
- Cursor is not described as resumable through this path in v1.0.30; it remains observation-only.
- The article does not generalize the bridge to every agent provider or every container runtime.
